guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): `CreatureCmd.Damage(ThrowingPlayerChoiceContext, Owner.Creature, HpLoss.BaseValue, Unblockable|Unpowered, null, null)` (FragrantMushroom.cs:31) vs `run.lose_hp(15)` (fragrant_mushroom.py:25)
guards.issue: MECHANISM: the source routes the 15 through the full damage command even out of combat, so the run-level Hook pipeline runs -- ModifyHpLostBeforeOsty / AfterOsty, the damage-received notifications, and the death check. RunState.lose_hp (run.py:294-302) runs ONLY the relic chain `modify_run_hp_loss` and then subtracts, so an out-of-combat HP loss fires no after-damage notification at all. DORMANT: the one modifier family that changes the NUMBER is present -- Tungsten Rod's ModifyHpLostAfterOsty maps to modify_run_hp_loss, which lose_hp does dispatch -- and the sim has no run-level HookSystem for the notification half, which is audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json's own finding (step 46, 'no run-level HookSystem'); one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3. The concrete thing that would make it live is porting a relic that reacts to HP LOSS rather than modifying it out of combat (Centennial Puzzle's on_damage_received is combat-only), or an out-of-combat block/thorns concept. Unblockable is a no-op out of combat on both sides, and lose_hp can take HP to 0 or below exactly as CreatureCmd.Damage can, so death behaviour agrees.
